$15.5 trillion in AUM following $869 billion of net inflows over the last twelve months, representing 10% organic base fee growth $205 billion of net inflows and 11% annualized organic base fee growth in the quarter reflect broad-based strength across iShares ® ETFs, systematic active equities, private markets, and cash 19% increase in revenue year-over-year reflects the positive impact of markets, organic base fee growth, higher performance fees, and higher technology services and subscription revenue 14% growth in technology services and subscription revenue year-over-year , driven by continued momentum in Aladdin® and multi-product solutions 19% increase in year-over-year GAAP operating income and 25% increase in GAAP diluted EPS impacted by a noncash change in fair value of contingent consideration associated with prior acquisitions, which has been excluded from as adjusted results 27% increase in year-over-year as adjusted operating income 38% increase in year-over-year as adjusted diluted EPS also reflects higher nonoperating income in the current quarter $550 million of share repurchases in the current quarter Laurence D. Fink, Chairman and CEO: “BlackRock's results demonstrate the value of our integrated platform, as clients increasingly choose us as a partner across investing, financing, and technology. That client trust is translating into higher earnings power, with shareholders benefiting from a more than 35% increase in adjusted earnings per share year-over-year, a 47.8% adjusted operating margin, and 11% annualized organic base fee growth in the third quarter. “BlackRock brings together issuer relationships built over decades, financing expertise, investment performance, and the technology and data that connect it all. That combination is differentiating us in every region in which we operate. It’s why BlackRock is winning mandates at the cutting edge of capital markets, from hyperscaler financings to pension outsourcings to Aladdin and Preqin partnerships. “Clients entrusted us with $205 billion of net inflows this quarter, and $869 billion over the last year. Our results reflect the scale of BlackRock, with 12% technology ACV growth and net inflows across every asset class, client type, region, and across active and index. Our track record of strong investment performance drove $66 billion of active net inflows, led by our fixed income and systematic franchises. iShares generated $135 billion of net inflows, diversified across categories and global product lines. “BlackRock’s ability to originate and structure at scale is leading to premier financing relationships and sourcing opportunities for our clients. We’ve raised $68 billion in private markets over the last twelve months, and our AI Infrastructure Partnership made its first deployment this quarter. “BlackRock is in a differentiated position as both a trusted advisor and destination for global client capital. That position is powering organic growth and value for our shareholders. We’re entering our seasonally strongest fourth quarter with accelerating momentum, and a broad pipeline spanning whole portfolio, private markets, retirement, and our international platforms. Demand for capital is growing across the global economy, and BlackRock is increasingly at the center of how that capital is deployed and managed. I’m confident in the opportunities that creates for our clients and in the long-term value we can generate for our shareholders.”

Historical periods have been recast to conform to this new presentation. Definitions: Total AUM: Alternative assets managed by BlackRock, which capture fair market value of investments and additional available capital. Fee-Paying AUM: Assets reported as AUM in BlackRock’s financial reports. Includes both invested capital and committed capital that is fee-paying in its commitment stage. Private Credit: Primarily represents direct lending, opportunistic and venture debt strategies. It does not include private credit assets across infrastructure and real estate debt, as well as assets in private placements and multi-strategy credit funds, which are reported within fixed income and multi-asset AUM. Liquid Alternatives: Includes hedge funds and hedge fund solutions (funds of funds). Liquid Credit: Active liquid credit strategies (such as high yield, bank loans, and collateralized loans) included in fixed income AUM. Note: Totals may not add due to rounding.
